summary: Eisei Kojima was a scholar of Buddhist studies. In 1976, he was attested as a professor at Ryukoku University and president of Doho University.
Eishu Miyazaki was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Rissho University (~1932–1938) under Gyōō Kageyama. He held posts at Minobusan University and Rissho University (~1950–1984).
Eishun Fushimi is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at the University of Hamburg (attested 1998) under David P. Jackson.

Eiun Hino is a Buddhist studies scholar who completed a master's course at the University of Tokyo (~2005–2007). He worked as a project researcher at the University of Tokyo (~2011–2014) and assistant professor at Musashino University (~2014–2019).

Ekai Kawaguchi worked in Buddhist studies and Tibetology, studying at Gyosei Shoin, Toyo University, Sera Monastery, and Central Hindu College, under teachers including Hiroshi Tsuchiya and Sarat Chandra Das. He held posts at Toyo University, Taisho University, and Toyo Bunko.
Eki Nakayama works in Buddhist studies. Attested in 2020, Nakayama studied at Kyoto University and held a DC2 special research fellowship with the Japan Society for the Promotion of Science.
Ekkyo Uno is a Buddhist studies scholar who served as a lecturer at Osaka University of Foreign Studies (attested 1991) and as a commissioned researcher at Honganji-ha Shogakuin (attested 1998).

Eleanor Rosch is a scholar of philosophy and Buddhist studies. She studied at Reed College (~1955–1959) and Harvard University (~1963–1969), and took up a post at the University of California, Berkeley, around 1971.
Elena De Rossi Filibeck is a Tibetology scholar. She has held posts at the University of Bonn and Sapienza University of Rome (attested 1997).
Elena France Hanson is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. She earned her PhD at Harvard University, where she was supervised by Charles Hallisey.

Elena Mucciarelli is an Indology scholar who studied at the University of Tübingen (~2008–2012) and later held posts there (2016–2017, attested 2022). In 2020, she was Assistant Professor for Hinduism in the Sanskrit Tradition and Gonda Lecturer at the University of Groningen.

Eli Franco is a scholar of Indology, philosophy, and Buddhist studies. He held posts at Kyoto University, La Trobe University, the Austrian Academy of Sciences, the University of Vienna, and served as institute director at Leipzig University.

Elijah Ary works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Sera Monastery, INALCO, and Harvard University (~2001–2007), where he earned a PhD supervised by Janet Gyatso and Leonard van der Kuijp, also studying under Charles Hallisey.

Eliot Deutsch was a scholar of philosophy and Indology who studied at Columbia University (~1956–1960). He edited Philosophy East and West (~1967–1988) and held posts at Harvard, Chicago, Cambridge, and the University of Hawaii.

Elisa Freschi is an Indologist and philosopher who earned her doctorate under Raffaele Torella (~2003–2006). She has held positions at Sapienza University of Rome, the Austrian Academy of Sciences, the Institute for the Cultural and Intellectual History of Asia, and the University of Vienna.

Elisabeth Schüssler Fiorenza is a scholar of religious studies who studied at the University of Würzburg (~1958–1963) and the University of Münster (~1965–1970). She held posts at the University of Notre Dame (~1970–1986) and Harvard University (~1986–2020).

Elizabeth Ann Cecil specializes in Indology, religious studies, and history/archaeology, earning degrees from Hastings College, University of Tennessee, and Brown University. She held posts at Baroda College, University of Groningen, Leiden University, and Florida State University.

Elizabeth English is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. She completed her PhD at the University of Oxford by 1999 under doctoral supervisor Alexis Sanderson, and also studied under Harunaga Isaacson.

Elizabeth Errington is a scholar of history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. She studied at SOAS University of London under Adrian David Hugh Bivar (~1980–1987) and served as a curator at the British Museum (~1992–2012).

Elizabeth Guthrie is a scholar of religious studies and Buddhist studies. She completed her PhD at the University of Canterbury (~1990–1994) and served as a tutor in Religious Studies at the University of Otago (~2004).
